findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5076 is 'Fix hostnames on UFs' and 5380 is 'Mattermost Alerts'. The VMware add-on is Splunk Add-on for VMware (3215); the Nutanix add-on in the catalogue is TA for Nutanix Prism (3103). The wrong IDs repeat in dataSources, references and detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: Splunk_TA_nutanix (5076) for Nutanix. Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere (5380) optional for VMFS.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite Splunk Add-on for VMware (3215) and TA for Nutanix Prism (3103) or the Prism Central TA (8349), or describe Nutanix collection as a custom poller.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for VMware emits datastore inventory as `vmware:inv:datastore` (and performance as `vmware:perf:datastore`); `vmware:vsphere:datastore` is not one of its sourcetypes.
findings.quote: optional `vmware:vsphere:datastore` (Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere, Splunkbase 5380)
findings.suggested_fix: Use `vmware:inv:datastore` from Splunk Add-on for VMware (3215) for VMFS capacity.

findings.explanation: vSAN space usage is normally read through the vSAN Management SDK (VsanSpaceReportSystem.QuerySpaceUsage) rather than a vSphere Automation REST path, and the listed Nutanix container fields (top-level `usage`, `effective_used_size_bytes`) and HyperFlex `dsName` / `usedCapacityInBytes` are not traceable to vendor API docs.
findings.quote: custom HEC `vmware:vsan:capacity` from vSphere REST `GET https://<vcenter>/api/vcenter/vsan/cluster/{cluster}/capacity` with `total_capacity_b`, `used_capacity_b`, `actual_used_capacity_b`, `slack_space_b`
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm each endpoint and field against the vSAN Management API, Prism v2 storage_containers (usage_stats.*) and HX Data Platform REST references, and name the real response paths.

findings.explanation: The implementation field is a benefits statement with no steps (pollers, lookups, schedule, alert condition), and it calls the output a 'health score' that the spl does not compute.
findings.quote: Delivers a single cross-vendor pool health score, tier and freeze aware, with a ticket payload that already contains `owner_email`
findings.suggested_fix: List the steps: deploy the four pollers or TAs, publish hci_pool_owner and hci_pool_growth_baseline, schedule every 10 minutes over -24h@h, and alert on severity_bucket critical/high.

findings.explanation: description lists data-sanity filters as alert conditions; the spl alerts on used% at or above 90/80 or ETA within 7/14 days (critical/high), growth above 3× baseline at >50% used (medium) and ≥60% used (low).
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the used-percent and ETA thresholds and the lookup overrides that drive severity_bucket.

findings.explanation: `python.version` only applies to Python scripted inputs, not a .sh wrapper, and a scripted input whose stdout is indexed with `sourcetype=vmware:vsan:capacity` conflicts with the text saying the poller posts to HEC (risking double ingestion). `TRUNCATE=0` disables truncation entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one path (scripted input writing to stdout, or a cron/HEC poller), drop python.version for shell scripts, and set a bounded TRUNCATE.

findings.explanation: Wrong add-on IDs and a nonexistent sourcetype mean the UC cannot have been validated end to end.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until each vendor arm is tested against real data.

findings.explanation: Cisco ACI fabric is unrelated to HCI pool capacity, and prerequisiteUseCases lists UC-19.1.1 (Cisco UCS server health), which this cross-vendor storage UC does not depend on.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace cisco_aci with HyperFlex / Nutanix / Azure Stack HCI models and drop the UC-19.1.1 prerequisite.

findings.explanation: Truncated HEC URL; no vendor API references for the four pool endpoints.
findings.suggested_fix: Link Data/UsetheHTTPEventCollector plus the vSAN, Prism, HX and Get-Volume documentation.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Each arm uses `earliest=-24h@h`, but `streamstats window=2016 current=f first(pool_used_bytes) AS used_7d_ago` expects 7 days of 5-minute samples; with only 24h of data, used_7d_ago is just the oldest sample of the day, so dgb_7d_roll = (≈1 day of growth)/7 and understates the fallback baseline about 7×, inflating growth_burst_factor and the medium tier. Widen the search window or read the 7-day baseline from a summary index.
During a change freeze, critical is demoted to medium even when the pool is ≥90% used or will be full within 7 days, which can suppress a real out-of-space page.
Comment macro restates sources and lookups rather than a short purpose line.

summary: A coherent cross-vendor pool-capacity design with clear severity tiers, but it cites two Splunkbase IDs that belong to unrelated apps and a VMware sourcetype that does not exist, and its 7-day growth baseline cannot be computed from the 24-hour search window.
